decision_conditions: Residential Quality - Internal FloorspaceThe proposed ground-floor flat, with a Gross Internal Area of 41 sqm, falls short of the Nationally Described Space Standards minimum of 50 sqm for a one-bedroom, two-person, single-storey dwelling. The proposed first-floor flat, with a Gross Internal Area of 56.08 sqm arranged over three storeys, falls short of the closest comparable Nationally Described Space Standards minimum of 58 sqm for a one-bedroom, two-person, two-storey dwelling, and is, in any event, configured in a manner (spanning three storeys) not envisaged as appropriate for a dwelling of this size and bedroom/person category. The proposal would therefore fail to provide either flat with an acceptable standard of living accommodation for future occupiers, contrary to Policy CP30 of the Council's Core Strategy and Policy DMD8 and DMD37 of the Council's Development Management Document, the Nationally Described Space Standards and London Plan Policy D6.

Residential Quality - Private Amenity SpaceThe proposed first-floor flat would not be provided with any private outdoor amenity space, contrary to the minimum requirement of 6 sqm for a two-person dwelling under the London Plan. Notwithstanding the amenity space nominally available to the ground floor flat, the submitted plans do not accurately or adequately demonstrate the extent, condition and usability of that space, or of the wider site, sufficient to conclude that an acceptable standard of residential amenity would be achieved for the development as a whole. The proposal is therefore contrary to Policy DMD8(g) and DMD9 of the Development Management Document, and the minimum private amenity space standards of the Policy D6 in London Plan.

Design, Character and Plan AccuracyThe dwelling has not been built in accordance with the plans and elevations approved under permission 21/00913/FUL, including unauthorised alterations to the fenestration and doors, the erection of a rear dormer, the erection of an outbuilding, and the loss of the approved grassed front garden and landscaped rear garden to hard-surfacing across the whole of both areas, contrary to Policy DMD8 and the objective of protecting the character of the surrounding area under Policies CP30, DMD37 and DMD11. Furthermore, the plans submitted with this application do not accurately reflect the dwelling as built and are internally inconsistent (including the submitted section showing a rear dormer that does not appear on the submitted rear elevation). The Local Planning Authority is unable to properly assess the design, scale and impact of these alterations on the character and appearance of the subject site and the area, or to confirm the floor areas and room layouts relied upon within the proposed flats would not provide a substandard form of accommodation prejudicial to the living conditions of future occupants. The proposal is therefore contrary to Policy CP30 of the Core Strategy and Policies DMD37, DMD13, DMD11 and DMD8 of the Development Management Document.

Landscaping, BNG, Inaccurate PlansThe proposal, due to the inaccurate submitted plans do not clearly identify the extent of existing and proposed hard and soft landscaping within the site. Consequently, insufficient information has been provided to assess the ecological impacts of the development, the retention and enhancement of habitats, and whether the proposal would deliver the required Biodiversity Net Gain. The proposal therefore fails to demonstrate compliance with Policy DMD8, DMD78, DMD79 and DMD81 of the Development Management Document and the Environment Act 2021 Biodiversity Net Gain.

Flood Risk and DrainageThe Flood Risk Assessment and Sustainable Drainage Strategy submitted in connection with this application relate to a different development (the erection of a new dwelling and single storey extension at No.39 Parkstone Avenue) and do not reflect the current condition of the application site, including the hard-surfacing of the front and rear gardens in place of the permeable, soft-landscaped garden approved under 21/00913/FUL. In the absence of an adequate, site-specific Drainage Strategy, and in the absence of any permeable paving or sustainable drainage measures serving the hard-surfaced areas, the Local Planning Authority cannot be satisfied that the proposal would not increase the rate and volume of surface water run-off from the site, contrary to Policies DMD8(i) and DMD61 of the Development Management Document and London Plan Policy SI13.
